\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عید} ('eyd)}{عید ('eyd)}]{\fa{عید} ('eyd) — a festival, a holiday; the New Year}

\label{lesson:FA-C339-eyd}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a will, then the Persian for an inheritance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عید}}
\textbf{\fa{عید}} (\emph{'eyd}) — \textquotedblleft{}a festival, a holiday; the New Year\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{برای} \fa{عید} \fa{همه} \fa{لباس} \fa{نو} \fa{میخرند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Barâ-ye 'eyd hame lebâs-e now mikharand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
For the New Year everyone buys new clothes.
\end{quote}

Said alone, \emph{'eyd} usually means Nowruz, the Persian New Year. \emph{'Eyd mobârak!} \textquotedblleft{}Happy holiday!\textquotedblright{}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{'eyd} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{'īd}, \textquotedblleft{}holiday, feast\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'eyd}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'eyd}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{'eyd}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a will, then the Persian for an inheritance, then say \emph{'eyd} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{عید} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A festival, a holiday; the New Year\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خانه} \fa{تکانی} (khâne tekâni)}{خانه تکانی (khâne tekâni)}]{\fa{خانه} \fa{تکانی} (khâne tekâni) — spring cleaning (before Nowruz)}

\label{lesson:FA-C339-khane-tekani}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an inheritance, then the Persian for a festival.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خانه} \fa{تکانی}}
\textbf{\fa{خانه} \fa{تکانی}} (\emph{khâne tekâni}) — \textquotedblleft{}spring cleaning (before Nowruz)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{قبل} \fa{از} \fa{عید} \fa{مادرم} \fa{خانه} \fa{تکانی} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Qabl az 'eyd mâdaram khâne tekâni mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Before the New Year my mother does the spring cleaning.
\end{quote}

Literally \textquotedblleft{}house-shaking\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{tekândan} \textquotedblleft{}to shake\textquotedblright{}: the whole house is cleaned before Nowruz.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khâne tekâni} is built from Persian \emph{khâne} \textquotedblleft{}house\textquotedblright{} and \emph{tekâni} \textquotedblleft{}shaking\textquotedblright{}, from the native verb \emph{tekândan} \textquotedblleft{}to shake\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khâne tekâni}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khâne tekâni}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{khâne tekâni}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for an inheritance, then the Persian for a festival, then say \emph{khâne tekâni} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سمنو} (samanu)}{سمنو (samanu)}]{\fa{سمنو} (samanu) — samanu, a sweet wheat pudding}

\label{lesson:FA-C339-samanu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a festival, then the Persian for spring cleaning.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سمنو}}
\textbf{\fa{سمنو}} (\emph{samanu}) — \textquotedblleft{}samanu, a sweet wheat pudding\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{سمنو} \fa{یکی} \fa{از} \fa{هفت} \fa{سین} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Samanu yeki az haft sin ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Samanu is one of the seven things on the haft-sin spread.
\end{quote}

A thick brown pudding of sprouted wheat, cooked for many hours; one of the \emph{haft sin}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{samanu} is a native Persian word. EtymDB lists it without a parent, and its origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{samanu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{samanu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a festival, then the Persian for spring cleaning, then say \emph{samanu} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سنجد} (senjed)}{سنجد (senjed)}]{\fa{سنجد} (senjed) — oleaster, a dried silver berry}

\label{lesson:FA-C339-senjed}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for spring cleaning, then the Persian for samanu.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سنجد}}
\textbf{\fa{سنجد}} (\emph{senjed}) — \textquotedblleft{}oleaster, a dried silver berry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{سنجد} \fa{هم} \fa{روی} \fa{سفره} \fa{هفت} \fa{سین} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Senjed ham ru-ye sofre-ye haft sin ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Oleaster is on the haft-sin spread too.
\end{quote}

The dried fruit of the oleaster tree; on the \emph{haft sin} it stands for love.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{senjed} is a native Persian word; EtymDB connects it with the Indo-European root \emph{spey-}, \textquotedblleft{}thorn-like\textquotedblright{}, fitting a thorny tree.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{senjed}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{senjed}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{senjed}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for spring cleaning, then the Persian for samanu, then say \emph{senjed} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ماهی} \fa{قرمز} (mâhi qermez)}{ماهی قرمز (mâhi qermez)}]{\fa{ماهی} \fa{قرمز} (mâhi qermez) — a goldfish}

\label{lesson:FA-C339-mahi-qermez}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for samanu, then the Persian for oleaster.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ماهی} \fa{قرمز}}
\textbf{\fa{ماهی} \fa{قرمز}} (\emph{mâhi qermez}) — \textquotedblleft{}a goldfish\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بچه} \fa{ها} \fa{ماهی} \fa{قرمز} \fa{را} \fa{در} \fa{تنگ} \fa{آب} \fa{گذاشتند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Bachche-hâ mâhi qermez râ dar tong-e âb gozâshtand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children put the goldfish in a bowl of water.
\end{quote}

Literally \textquotedblleft{}red fish\textquotedblright{}. A goldfish in a bowl sits on the Nowruz table.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mâhi} \textquotedblleft{}fish\textquotedblright{} is inherited from Middle Persian \emph{māhīg} (EtymDB). \emph{qermez} \textquotedblleft{}red\textquotedblright{} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{qirmiz}, \textquotedblleft{}crimson, kermes\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), named after a red dye.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
